title: Jackknife Receptors & Organ-Size Brakes: Integrin Inside-Out/Outside-In Mechanotransduction, FAK & the Hippo–LATS–YAP/TAZ–TEAD Pathway — Neonatal LAD-I (ITGB2/CD18), LAD-III (FERMT3/Kindlin-3) & Glanzmann thrombasthenia (αIIbβ3), natalizumab CNS PML vs. gut-selective vedolizumab, NF2-loss mesothelioma & stiff-matrix mechanotransduction, 1-Å crystal walks inside αIIbβ3 (3FCS), FAK FERM–kinase (2J0M), YAP–TEAD1 + buried palmitate P1L344 (3KYS) & TEAD1–K-975 covalent Cys359 (7CMM), arterial catch-bond & Young's-modulus calculations, oral GPIIb/IIIa partial-agonist failure vs. zalunfiban (RUC-4), FDA-approved Kresladi & defactinib + avutometinib, and clinical TEAD inhibitors (VT3989, IAG933, GNE-7883) targeting EGFR/KRAS drug-tolerant persisters

teenKit.tldr: Your body isn't a bag of floating chemical soup—it's a tensegrity masterpiece where physical forces like pulling, stretching, and squeezing dictate whether cells live, bleed, or turn cancerous.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how cells feel physical force unlocks advanced treatments for deadly organ-size errors, unstoppable bleeding disorders, and drug-resistant cancers.
keyTakeaways: Cells use molecular levers like integrins to connect their internal cytoskeletons directly to the outside world, turning mechanical tension into chemical commands.
The Hippo pathway acts as an organ-size brake, using mechanical stiffness to tell cells when to stop growing or when to multiply out of control.
Tiny atomic-level mutations in structural proteins can cause catastrophic medical mysteries, from pus-free infections to dangerous, un-coagulable bleeding.

vocab.meaning: The cellular process of converting physical forces like stretching or fluid shear stress into biochemical signals.
A physical jackknife receptor that spans the cell membrane, locking the cell's interior skeleton to the extracellular matrix.
A master signaling network that acts as an organ-size brake by sequestering growth-promoting proteins when tissues become too crowded or soft.
A unique molecular bond that paradoxically grips tighter and lasts longer when physical pulling force is applied to it.

quiz.question: What is the fundamental flaw in the traditional 'passive soup model' of cellular biology according to the episode?
options: Cells actually float in a gel-like jelly instead of a liquid soup.
It treats cells as passive bags of drifting molecules, ignoring how physical forces and mechanical tension drive cellular behavior.
It incorrectly claims that hormones are too large to travel through blood.
It states that proteins never interact with each other without electric fields.
quiz.explanation: The podcast shatters the textbook illusion by showing that cells are constantly pulled, sheared, and squeezed, turning mechanical force into vital biological decisions.

quiz.question: Why did a newborn with a severe infection display a complete lack of pus at the wound site in the LAD-I case study?
options: The baby's white blood cells lacked the integrin receptors needed to grip blood vessel walls and crawl out into the infected tissue.
The infection was caused by a virus that completely prevents white blood cell production.
The baby's body temperature was too low to generate white blood cells.
Pus is only produced in adults, never in newborns.
quiz.explanation: Neonatal LAD-I involves a defect in ITGB2/CD18 integrins, meaning neutrophils cannot anchor or migrate out of the bloodstream to form pus at an infection site.

quiz.question: How does a stiff, scar-like extracellular matrix (such as in asbestos-scarred lungs) promote aggressive tumor growth?
options: By physically blocking chemotherapy drugs from entering the bloodstream.
By releasing toxic heavy metals that mutate cellular DNA.
By mechanically triggering survival pathways like FAK and disabling the Hippo pathway's organ-size brakes.
By freezing the cells so they can no longer undergo apoptosis.
quiz.explanation: A stiff matrix exerts physical tension that activates focal adhesion kinases and inactivates the Hippo pathway, signaling cells to keep dividing relentlessly.
